## Leakage Flag

## Metric Conventions

- Task: within-user ranking (each user's impressions ranked against each other)
- nDCG@5: sorts by score with a stable sort (ties fall back to row order)
- AUC: averages ranks over ties (Mann-Whitney U)
- GAUC: per-user AUC, only users with 0 < positives < impressions,
  weighted by positive count
- Zero-positive users: nDCG recorded as 0.0 and included in the average
- Primary score = mean(GAUC, nDCG@5)

## Measured Dead Ends

- Adding all 13 static feature fields: primary 0.5940 vs 0.5950 for the default 5
- Embedding dimension k = 8 / 16 / 32: primary 0.5895 / 0.5902 / 0.5887 (flat)
- The bottleneck is not features or capacity
- First-order user-only terms contribute exactly 0 to within-user ranking
  (any term constant within a user does not change intra-group ordering)

feature_candidates.description: Categorical feature quantizing hourmin into 6-hour buckets (0-6,6-12,12-18,18-24) as user-independent or user-specific propensity, fit on train-only distribution.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures user viewing rhythm; if user-level interaction with bucket is stable, can lift GAUC/nDCG by adding ranking context beyond static features.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute train-only user-hour-bucket long_view propensity (or raw bucket one-hot); encode as categorical embedding in feature pipeline (src.models.features). No future-user exposure.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if computed on train only; must avoid valid/test-derived aggregation.
feature_candidates.name: hourmin_bucket

feature_candidates.description: Per-user, per-tab long_view rate computed from the user's train history (smoothed with a prior); used as a ranking bias feature.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Provides user-specific tab affinity; likely stronger than a single tab dummy because user-preferred tabs differ, improving within-user separation.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Aggregate train rows by (user_id, tab) to get long_view rate with smoothing (e.g., Bayes/Laplace); join to all rows. Must be computed before any validation use.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Safe if train-only; must not use valid/test exposure or label info.
feature_candidates.name: user_tab_longview_propensity

feature_candidates.description: For each user-video impression, minutes/events since last exposure to the same video (or same category), decayed exponentially, summarizing within-session recency.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Recent repeat exposure often suppresses re-watching; decayed recency could add strong negative signal for long_view within user sessions.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Scan train rows per user in chronological order, maintain last-seen timestamp/video count for each video and category; produce exponential decay feature; validate against log ordering.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Medium if time-order is respected; leaks if derived with future exposures.
feature_candidates.name: decayed_video_recency

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Tab Breakdown (train): tab-shared rates differ by >30x across tabs, with most traffic on tabs 1 and 4.
findings.implication: User-specific tab long-view propensities (computed from train only) may outperform a single global tab bias, providing discriminative signal for within-user ranking.
findings.observation: Long-view rate ranges from 0.42% (tab 3) to 61.25% (tab 10); tab 1 (38.61%) and tab 4 (48.93%) dominate exposure, indicating per-tab user propensity likely separates ranking within users.
findings.title: Tab long-view rates vary widely

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Data Quality: hourmin encodes hour times 100 in UTC+8; label rates vary by tab, and no hour rate table is supplied; hypothesis only.
findings.implication: A quantized hourmin categorical feature (registered under history_features) could improve ranking if user-specific hour patterns differ, but needs train-only aggregation to avoid future-user leakage.
findings.observation: hourmin encodes hour times 100 in UTC+8; whole-day interaction availability suggests bucketing into 0-6/6-12/12-18/18-24 could expose stable user rhythms, but within-user reordering across sessions must be avoided.
findings.title: Temporal hourmin may capture viewing rhythm

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Leakage Flag and Measured Dead Ends: static feature sets did not beat default 5; embedding capacity is flat.
findings.implication: Spatial/static stats are unlikely to push primary past 0.6016; temporal and interaction-based features are more promising and reduce leakage risk if leaky stats are excluded.
findings.observation: The video statistics table is a full-platform period aggregate (ratio ~4892:1) and legal; its within-user rank correlation would require a train-only correlation matrix, but dead-end experiments show static features flat at 0.594-0.595.
findings.title: Leaky video stats show limited within-user value

data.recommended_next_focus: Run an ablation adding hourmin_bucket and user_tab_longview_propensity (both train-only) on top of the default 5 features; if GAUC/nDCG improves, then test decayed_video_recency under history_features.
data.summary: EDA plan targets leakage-safe within-user features for long_view ranking: hourmin bucket, per-tab user propensity, and decayed recency. Baseline primary is 0.6016; static features and embedding capacity are dead ends, suggesting interaction/temporal signals matter.
ui_notes: Tab propensity and hourmin bucket are cheap to implement and likely leakage-safe; prioritize them.
